title: Initiating a Project in Context

header.html: 4.3.1 carry out initiating a project: activities, inputs and outputs; recommended roles and responsibilities; how the practices are applied; 4.3.2 analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, using the purpose and objectives, the practices and tailoring
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

html:
1Purpose, objectives and context

The initiating a project process builds solid foundations, so the organization understands the work needed to deliver the project's products before committing to significant spend. It takes place in the initiation stage, which the board authorized at the end of start-up.

In plain words, the objectives are:

  • Everyone agrees what the project is to achieve, why, how, by whom and at what cost, quality and risk.
  • The business case is refined, and the plans and tolerances support it.
  • The approaches and controls are set and tailored to the project.
  • A baseline, the PID, is ready for the board's decision to authorize the project.

The process serves ensure continued business justification, learn from experience, define roles, responsibilities and relationships, manage by stages, focus on products and tailor to suit the project.

Exam tip

. Initiating produces the PID; starting up produced the project brief. The PID is the baseline the board decides on and the project is controlled against.

2Activities, inputs and outputs

Activity names are given in general terms. The Official Book's wording may differ slightly, so learn what each activity achieves.

Activity What it achieves
Prepare the management approaches One approach for each area: benefits, sustainability, commercial, quality, risk, issues, communication, change, digital and data
Set up the project controls Tolerances, reporting, decision points and logs, so the project can be controlled
Plan the project The project plan, the project product description and the stage structure, with estimates and a schedule
Refine the business case A detailed case that uses the real costs and timescale from the plan
Assemble the PID One baseline document set that the board can decide on
Direction Items
Inputs Authority to initiate; the project brief; the initiation stage plan; the project log and lessons from start-up; corporate standards
Outputs The PID; the plan for the next stage, prepared for the board; the updated project log, including the lessons log
Exam tip

. The board needs both the PID and the next stage plan to authorize the project. An approach that sends only the PID, or only a plan for the next stage, is incomplete.

3Roles and responsibilities

The project manager leads this process, and the board decides on the result. Learn each focus and check the Official Book's responsibility table.

Role Focus in initiating
Executive Accountable for the refined business case and for the justified project the board will decide on
Senior user Accountable for the user need: acceptance criteria and how benefits will be measured
Senior supplier Makes sure the supplier side of the plan, estimates and commercial approach is realistic
Project manager Prepares the approaches, controls and plan; refines the case with the executive; assembles the PID
Project assurance Independently checks that the PID is sound and consistent
Project support Builds the document set, sets up the tools, filing and project log
Corporate or programme management Provides the standards and the project tolerances the PID must respect
Exam tip

. The project manager prepares; the board owns the decision. Each board member answers for their own interest in the PID, and assurance checks but does not approve.

4How the practices are applied

Practice Applied in initiating
Business case Refined business case; benefits management and sustainability management approaches
Organization Team structure, role descriptions and commercial management approach
Plans Project plan, project product description, plan for the next stage; detail for the next stage only
Quality Quality management approach; product descriptions for the main products; quality and product registers started
Risk Risk management approach; risk register reviewed with owners and responses
Issues Issue management approach, with change control, change authority and any change budget
Progress Tolerances, reporting and controls; digital and data management approach; lessons log
Exam tip

. Every practice has a product in the PID, and the plans and tolerances must agree with the business case. If the plan costs more than the benefits justify, the case must be revisited, not hidden.

5Judging the process

What effective initiating looks like Red flag, with the principle
A PID that is the baseline for decisions and control A PID written, filed and never used or updated (business justification)
Approaches tailored and proportionate A full template copied without thought, or approaches missing (tailor)
Plans and tolerances consistent with the business case Cost above what the benefits justify, or tolerances wider than the corporate limits (business justification)
A product-based plan with acceptance criteria An activity list with no project product description (focus on products)
Detail for the next stage, outline for later ones Every stage planned in detail months ahead (manage by stages)
A business case refined with real costs and benefit owners The brief's case copied unchanged (business justification)
Roles and stakeholders agreed and described Unclear roles; key stakeholders missing from the communication approach (define roles)
Lessons from start-up used Earlier lessons ignored (learn from experience)

Tailoring makes the PID proportionate, not smaller than the need.

Setting How initiating changes
Small project A short PID; approaches as brief paragraphs or a reference to organization standards
Agile or hybrid delivery The PID records iteration length, how the backlog is controlled and how tolerances apply to each time-box
Large or multi-supplier project Separate, formal approach documents; a detailed commercial management approach; links to the programme
Sustainability, digital and data concerns Targets and data protection set out in the approaches
Exam tip

. Judge a PID by whether it is fit to decide on, not by its length. A two-page PID can be effective; a hundred pages that nobody reads is not.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Sam Okafor's PID for Project Harbor plans all four stages in full detail, including the rollout stage, to give the board confidence. Was this an appropriate action, and why?

  • AYes, because a fully detailed plan for every stage is the strongest baseline for the board
  • BYes, because the board can only authorize the project if every stage is planned in detail
  • CNo, because later stages should be outlined, with detail kept for the stage ahead
  • DNo, because the PID should hold only the next stage plan and no plan for the project
Show the answer

Answer: C. The planning horizon limits reliable detail to the next stage, while the PID still holds an outline project plan.

S2While refining the business case for Project Harbor, Sam finds that the plan costs 530,000, not the 480,000 in the project brief. What should Sam do?

  • AUpdate the business case with the higher cost and tell the executive before the decision
  • BTrim the estimates until the plan fits within the 480,000 shown in the project brief
  • CLeave the business case unchanged and record the new cost only in the daily log for now
  • DAsk the board to authorize the project now and discuss the cost during the first stage
Show the answer

Answer: A. The business case must be refined with real costs and the executive must know before the decision, in line with continued business justification.

S3Sam wants to confirm that the acceptance criteria in Project Harbor's project product description will give permit users what they need. Who should confirm this?

  • AThe senior supplier, Lena Kovac
  • BThe executive, Marta Quinn
  • CThe project manager, Sam Okafor
  • DThe senior user, Tomas Reyes
Show the answer

Answer: D. The senior user is accountable for the user need and for how well the products meet it.

S4Which management product records how the benefits of Project Harbor will be measured, when, and by whom?

  • AThe commercial management approach in the PID
  • BThe benefits management approach in the PID
  • CThe quality management approach in the PID
  • DThe project product description in the PID
Show the answer

Answer: B. The benefits management approach covers how and when benefits are measured and who is responsible, while the other products cover contracts, quality and the product itself.

S5Wei Chen's team will deliver Project Harbor in iterations. Sam records in the PID the iteration length, how the backlog is controlled and how tolerances apply to each time-box. Was this an appropriate action, and why?

  • ANo, because iteration details belong only in the team's plans and should stay out of the PID
  • BNo, because tailoring is decided by the supplier and is not recorded in the PID
  • CYes, because an iterative project needs no business case or project plan in the PID
  • DYes, because initiating tailors the approaches to the delivery method and shows control
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tailoring decisions are recorded in the PID so the board sees how the project will be controlled, and the business case and plan are still needed.

S6Sam has assembled the PID for Project Harbor and Aisha Bello has reviewed it. What should Sam do next?

  • AGive the PID and the next stage plan to the board so it can decide on the project
  • BStart the first build work packages because project assurance has reviewed the PID
  • CSend the PID to Delta Software so that it can sign the contract for the build stage
  • DFile the PID until the build stage is over and then bring it up to date with changes
Show the answer

Answer: A. The board authorizes the project on the PID and the next stage plan, and assurance review is a check, not an authorization.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of initiating a project?

Show the answer

To build solid foundations so the organization understands the work needed before committing to significant spend.

R2What is the main output of initiating a project?

Show the answer

The project initiation documentation (PID).

R3Name two activities of initiating in general terms.

Show the answer

Preparing the management approaches, setting up the project controls, planning the project, refining the business case, or assembling the PID.

R4Which two products from start-up are the inputs that authorize this process?

Show the answer

The project brief and the initiation stage plan.

R5Who decides whether to authorize the project after initiating?

Show the answer

The project board.

R6Where are tailoring decisions recorded?

Show the answer

In the PID.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose solid foundations before significant spend
Inputs project brief, initiation stage plan, project log, lessons
Outputs the PID and the next stage plan
Activities approaches, controls, project plan, refined case, assemble the PID
Roles project manager prepares; executive, senior user and senior supplier answer for their interest
Judging baseline used, proportionate approaches, plans and tolerances match the case
Tailoring proportionate PID; record how the delivery method is controlled
